knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific guardrails and patterns for Dart. Loaded when agents work on .dart files, pubspec.yaml, or Flutter/server-side Dart projects. Applies to Dart 3.0+ with sound null safety.

core-principles.principle: The type system guarantees non-nullable by default; nullable types are explicit.
Use Futures, Streams, and async/await for all I/O and event-driven logic.
Prefer final locals, const constructors, and immutable data structures.
Use mixins, extension methods, and sealed class hierarchies.
Follow official Effective Dart style for naming, documentation, and API design.

guardrail.rule: Never use ! (null assertion) without a preceding null check or compile-time guarantee. A runtime null assertion failure is a crash.
guardrail.bad: // BAD: crashes at runtime if null final name = json['name'] as String;

guardrail.rule: Always await Futures or return them. Never fire-and-forget without error handling.
Use Dart 3.0+ with sound null safety. Never add // @dart=2.x opt-out comments.
Set timeouts on all external calls using .timeout(Duration(...)). Catch specific exceptions, not bare catch (e).
Use late only when initialization is guaranteed before first access. Never use late as a substitute for nullable or Optional.
guardrail.bad: // BAD: late used for laziness without guarantees late final String config;

guardrail.rule: Run dart format . before every commit (80-char line length). Run dart analyze with strict mode before committing. Zero analyzer warnings on commit.
Use final for all local variables that are not reassigned. Use const constructors for compile-time constant objects.
Use ? for nullable types only at API boundaries (JSON, platform channels). Prefer ?? and ?. over explicit null checks inside the application.
Pin dependency versions with caret syntax (^1.2.0) for libraries, exact for apps. Run dart pub outdated periodically.

directory.purpose: CLI entry points for command-line apps

project-structure.note: lib/src/ is private; export public API from lib/my_package.dart. No business logic in main.dart — delegate to services.

pattern.name: Records and Pattern Matching (Dart 3)
pattern.description: Records provide lightweight immutable tuples with named fields. Switch expressions with patterns enable exhaustive matching.

pattern.name: Sealed Classes and Exhaustive Matching
pattern.description: Sealed classes create closed type hierarchies. The compiler enforces that all subtypes are handled in switch expressions.

pattern.description: Use Isolate.run for CPU-intensive work that would block the event loop.

testing.framework: package:test for pure Dart; package:flutter_test for widgets; package:mockito with @GenerateMocks for type-safe mocking

rules.rule: Test files: *_test.dart in test/ mirroring lib/src/ structure
Test names describe behavior: 'returns empty list when no users exist'
Use setUp() not setUpAll() for mutable state

tooling.commands: dart format . # Format all Dart files dart analyze # Static analysis (lint + type checks) dart test # Run all tests dart test --coverage=coverage # Run tests with coverage dart run bin/main.dart # Run CLI application dart compile exe bin/main.dart # AOT compile to native executable dart pub get # Install dependencies dart pub outdated # Check for dependency updates dart pub deps # Show dependency tree dart fix --apply # Auto-apply suggested fixes
tooling.analysis-options:
# analysis_options.yaml include: package:lints/recommended.yaml
analyzer: language: strict-casts: true strict-inference: true strict-raw-types: true errors: missing_return: error dead_code: warning
linter: rules: - prefer_final_locals - prefer_const_constructors - prefer_const_declarations - avoid_dynamic_calls - unawaited_futures - always_declare_return_types - annotate_overrides - avoid_print - prefer_single_quotes - require_trailing_commas - unnecessary_lambdas - prefer_expression_function_bodies
